challenges.title: Two Sum
challenges.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
challenges.constraints:
• 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
• -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
• -10^9 <= target <= 10^9
• Only one valid answer exists.
challenges.editorial:
### Dynamic Hash Map O(N) Solution

By using a Hash Map (Object), we can keep track of the complement values we are searching for as we iterate through the list. For each number `nums[i]`, we calculate its complement `target - nums[i]`. If the complement exists in our map, we have found our pair and return their indices. Otherwise, we store the current number index in our map and continue.

**Complexity Analysis:**
- **Time Complexity:** O(N) because we iterate through the array of size N exactly once.
- **Space Complexity:** O(N) since in the worst case we store up to N elements in our hash map.

challenges.title: Reverse String
challenges.description:
Write a function that takes a string `s` and returns it reversed.

For example, if the input is `"hello"`, the output should be `"olleh"`.
challenges.constraints:
• 1 <= s.length <= 10^5
• s consists of printable ASCII characters.
challenges.editorial:
### Two-Pointer Swap or String Reversion O(N)

In JavaScript, we can split the string into an array, reverse the array in place, and join it back. Alternatively, we can use a two-pointer approach swapping items from the start and end until they meet in the middle.

**Complexity Analysis:**
- **Time Complexity:** O(N) where N is the length of the string.
- **Space Complexity:** O(N) to store the reversed characters in memory.

challenges.title: Fizz Buzz
challenges.description:
Given an integer `n`, return a string array answer (1-indexed) where:
- `answer[i] == "FizzBuzz"` if `i` is divisible by 3 and 5.
- `answer[i] == "Fizz"` if `i` is divisible by 3.
- `answer[i] == "Buzz"` if `i` is divisible by 5.
- `answer[i] == "i"` (as a string) if none of the above conditions are true.
challenges.editorial:
### Direct Divisibility Checks O(N)

We iterate from 1 up to `n`, running division checks. It is essential to test divisibility by 15 (both 3 and 5) first, or concatenate strings (`"Fizz"` + `"Buzz"`) dynamically to avoid missing the combined conditions.

**Complexity Analysis:**
- **Time Complexity:** O(N) since we perform a constant number of operations for each integer from 1 to N.
- **Space Complexity:** O(N) to hold our returned array of string answers.

challenges.title: Fibonacci Number
challenges.description:
The Fibonacci numbers, commonly denoted `F(n)` form a sequence, called the Fibonacci sequence, such that each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1. That is:
- `F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1`
- `F(n) = F(n - 1) + F(n - 2)`, for `n > 1`.

Given `n`, calculate `F(n)`.
challenges.editorial:
### Dynamic Programming (Space-Optimized Iteration) O(N)

Instead of costly recursion O(2^N), we can compute Fibonacci iteratively. By storing only the last two values (`a` and `b`), we can update them in a loop, reducing auxiliary space to O(1).

**Complexity Analysis:**
- **Time Complexity:** O(N) since we iterate from 2 up to N.
- **Space Complexity:** O(1) auxiliary space as we only store the two preceding terms.
